not_found: Hyperfine A constants of 103Rh (I=1/2, no B): measured for the eight lowest levels a 4F9/2,7/2,5/2,3/2, a 2D5/2,3/2 and 4d8 5s 2F7/2,5/2 by atomic-beam magnetic resonance (Chan, Childs, Goodman, Phys. Rev. 173, 107 (1968)) and for 28 further states including all drawn 4d8 5p z 4D, 4G, 4F, 2G, 2F, 2D levels by laser-rf double resonance / high-resolution laser spectroscopy (Bengtsson, Fraenkel, Olsson, Z. Phys. D 5, 147 (1987)). Only the abstract pages and the 2-page Springer preview could be opened (https://journals.aps.org/pr/abstract/10.1103/PhysRev.173.107, https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF01436889); the tables with the numbers are behind paywalls, so NO A values are given here.
Measured Landé g_J factors of the eight lowest Rh I levels (Chan, Childs, Goodman 1968, atomic beam): paper not accessible; the NIST levels file carries Landé g values for all drawn levels.
Lifetimes of the even-parity metastable levels a 4F7/2,5/2,3/2 and a 2D5/2,3/2: no measurement located.
Salih, Duquette, Lawler 1983 (PRA 27, 1193): original table not opened; its 22 lifetimes are taken second-hand from Table 2 of Malcheva et al. 2015.

Measured transition probabilities newer or more precise than NIST: none located. NIST Rh I A values (tp_ref T5181, 110 lines) are the experimental branching-fraction results of Duquette & Lawler, J. Opt. Soc. Am. B 2, 1948 (1985) (code resolved in the NIST bibliographic database). Malcheva et al. 2015 Table 5 and Li et al., MNRAS 503, 5085 (2021, high-lying levels, not opened) give only calculated gA values.
Precise (laser / frequency-comb) transition frequencies of Rh I: none located.
Isotope shifts: not applicable for natural Rh (103Rh is the only stable isotope).
Lines used for laser cooling / precision work in Rh I: no experiment located.
conflicts: Rh I 4d8 5p z 4G°7/2 (31101.75 cm-1) lifetime: 9.2(0.4) ns [Malcheva] vs 8.6(0.4) ns [Salih] differ by more than the combined uncertainty
Rh I 4d8 5p z 2F°7/2 (32004.01 cm-1) lifetime: 9.4(0.5) ns [Kwiatkowski] vs 8.7(0.4) ns [Salih] differ by more than the combined uncertainty
Rh I 4d8 5p z 4F°3/2 (32277.43 cm-1) lifetime: 9.5(0.5) ns [Kwiatkowski] vs 8.7(0.4) ns [Salih] differ by more than the combined uncertainty
Rh I 4d8 5p z 2D°3/2 (33867.04 cm-1) lifetime: 7.7(0.4) ns [Malcheva] vs 7(0.3) ns [Salih] differ by more than the combined uncertainty
Rh I 4d8 5p z 2D°3/2 (33867.04 cm-1) lifetime: 7.6(0.4) ns [Kwiatkowski] vs 7(0.3) ns [Salih] differ by more than the combined uncertainty
Rh I 4d8 5p y 4D°7/2 (36787.48 cm-1) lifetime: 10.3(0.6) ns [Kwiatkowski] vs 11.3(0.6) ns [Salih] differ by more than the combined uncertainty
Rh I y 4D°1/2 (38474.43 cm-1): measured lifetime 17.1(9) ns (Salih 1983 via Malcheva 2015) vs HFR+CPOL theory 12.8 ns
notes: Rh has a single stable isotope, 103Rh (I=1/2), so there are no isotope shifts and no electric-quadrupole B constants. All lifetimes are time-resolved laser-induced-fluorescence values. Entry choice per level: Malcheva et al. 2015 where they measured the level (17 levels); otherwise Kwiatkowski et al. 1982 (original scan opened, 13 levels); otherwise Salih et al. 1983 as quoted by Malcheva et al. (method "compilation"). Remaining measurements and the HFR+CPOL theory value are under lifetime.alternatives. Kwiatkowski et al. print level energies rounded to 1 cm-1; they were matched to the NIST energies by designation. Malcheva et al. state uncertainties "include the statistical uncertainties as well as the variation of the results between the repeated measurements"; Kwiatkowski et al. error limits are statistical deviations plus time-calibration uncertainty. Malcheva et al. write that four levels were measured in all three experiments, but their Table 2 shows three such levels (31101.75, 33867.04, 36787.48 cm-1); 35333.85 cm-1 has only Salih + Malcheva. The transitions list is empty on purpose: nothing measured beyond what NIST ASD already holds was found. Levels above 36000 cm-1 are included although not drawn on the site.
